decisions.scope: Repository organization across CLI, ESLint plugin, tests, scripts, documentation, and CI support
decisions.decision: This repository uses dedicated config/ and types/ ownership across every package and support subsystem. Constants are grouped by behavior under config/; types are under types/. Shipped configuration assets stay under packages/cli/configurations/ and parsing and schemas stay under parsers/ owners. This overrides diagram recommendations to delete config/ and types/. Consumer repositories have no dedicated-folder requirement.
evidence: Explicit user corrections in this conversation

decisions.decision: The current user plan requires four test directories: cli, plugin, tools, and packages. Config and types mirror their behavioral owners, and the shared harness stays flat. Scripts own suite and registry orchestration. This supersedes the inherited five-family decision.
evidence: The user’s implementation plan in this conversation

decisions.scope: Coverage levels, automatic applicable configurations, and native rule generation
decisions.decision: Recommended and all are the only developer-facing coverage levels. Remove opt-in selection fields, prompts, and extra_checks without replacing them. Security, duplication, and licenses follow repository applicability and the chosen level. Remove Vulture entirely. Native-tool configuration syntax remains generated from these two levels. Retain legitimate prerequisites.
evidence: User implementation plan: Finish all findings with only recommended and all, Decisions.

decisions.scope: Automatic applicable configuration selection and manual language/framework overrides
decisions.decision: Retain gspot add/remove, init --configurations, and authored configuration lists for manual language and framework overrides. Remove opt-in check controls such as security, duplication, and licenses flags. This clarifies recommended-and-all: these remain the only check-coverage levels; language/framework overrides remain project configuration.

decisions.decision: The CLI commands are init, install, apply, check, set, add, remove, export, ignore, list, explain, and doctor. They are the commands gspot needs. Findings may change how a command works, but not the set.

decisions.decision: A repository that customizes gspot (tools, exceptions, and other settings) can export a template from its installation, and another repository can install gspot from that template file. The template feature stays and must carry that customization.
evidence: Owner statement in the review request of October 6, 2026

decisions.decision: One setting for each concern across the repository. No special time limits, per-suite or per-OS budgets, environment switches, or options for one caller or one situation. When something is slow or special, fix the cause.
evidence: Owner statement of October 6, 2026 about the 60 s and 900 s test limits

decisions.decision: The owner rejects the current gspot.toml shape: mixed [table], [[array]], dotted keys, and inline tables; one repeated header for each entry; scattered sections; unclear names such as naming.fixed_keys. gspot.toml must be consistent, readable, grouped by concern, and clearly named. The target format is the one in findings/review/policy-format.md, section "The target format" (adopted on October 6, 2026, in the answers of findings/review/owner-questions.md).
evidence: Owner statement in the review request of October 6, 2026

decisions.decision: gspot ships only as JavaScript on npm. Delete the per-OS standalone archives and everything that builds, tests, verifies, uploads, pins, or documents them. They must never come back: no compiled archives, no platform packages, no release assets, no GitHub archive pin in mise. Under run_with = "mise", gspot pins itself through the mise npm backend. Commit 4ce293ae8 reintroduced them against the decision of September 29, 2026.

Restore the agent rule TALKING.md ("When you talk, use ASD-STE100.") in every installation, at both levels, as before commit 4ce293ae8. Delete the sentence that replaced it in WRITING.md ("Your replies to the user follow these rules: short sentences, active voice, and one idea per sentence.").

Every banned term and group that commits 65927b452 and 4fbe75989 removed or made removable comes back and ships. No group is removable. The banned-term checks run at level all only; level recommended does not run them.
The documentation site and the policy schema move from gspot.dev to generativespotting.com (all lowercase, one word). The site still deploys to Cloudflare Workers.

Delete Verdaccio. Tests pack the workspace packages once per run and serve them from the one small local npm registry gspot already has, moved into tests/harness. A temporary .npmrc routes only the @gspothq scope to that server; every other package comes from the npm registry through the normal cache. Only runs that install the private tool project start it. The same server, with a token, keeps testing private-registry credentials, and the small Python index stays only for the private-index credential tests.
evidence: The owner delegated this design on October 6, 2026

decisions.decision: The workflows use no GitHub environments. The release starts by hand, so it needs no approval gate. The docs deploy reads the two Cloudflare values as repository secrets.

decisions.scope: Markdown, JSON, and YAML tools in every stack
decisions.decision: gspot runs on Node.js or Bun in every repository, so the Node-based tools for Markdown, JSON, and YAML (Prettier, markdownlint-cli2, v8r) stay the one tool set for those files in every stack. gspot pins them only when an active check uses them. Records that asked for other tools in Python or Swift projects are superseded. A repository without a JavaScript configuration gets no Prettier or markdownlint files at its root (areas/developer-experience/021).
evidence: Follows the npm-only decision of October 6, 2026 and the owner rule of one setting per concern; settled by Claude at the owner's request
